relations.subject: cbl:replication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted dependsOnService shape fits CBL's replicator depending on the Sync Gateway product to function at all
relations.evidence: It does so by using a replicator to interact with Sync Gateway.

relations.subject: cbl:user-authorization
relations.evidence: By default, Sync Gateway does not enable user authorization. This makes it easier to get up and running with synchronization.

relations.subject: cbl:server-authentication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted usesEnum shape; the three named certificate-verification modes (CA Cert / Self-Signed Cert / Pinned Certificate) form a closed set
relations.evidence: If there is a pinned certificate, nothing else matters, the server cert must exactly match the pinned certificate. If there are no pinned certs and setAcceptOnlySelfSignedServerCertificate is true then any self-signed certificate is accepted... If there are no pinned certificates and setAcceptOnlySelfSignedServerCertificate is false (default), the client validates the server's certificates against the system CA certificates.

relations.subject: cbl:client-authentication
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted usesEnum shape; two named authenticator types form a closed set - structurally echoes Capella's credential-type-keyed privilege model (per the round-2 registry note) but serves a different purpose: proving client identity to Sync Gateway, not gating management-plane operations
relations.evidence: There are two ways to authenticate from a Couchbase Lite client: Basic Authentication or Session Authentication.

relations.subject: cbl:certificate-pinning
relations.evidence: This all assumes that you have configured the Sync Gateway to provide the appropriate SSL certificates, and have included the appropriate certificate in your app bundle — for more on this see: [Certificate Pinning](#lbl-cert-pinning).

relations.subject: cbl:auto-purge-on-revoke
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused loosely - the purge is triggered by a channel-access-revocation decision made entirely on the Sync Gateway side; CBL only reacts to it
relations.evidence: By default, when a user loses access to a channel all documents in the channel (that do not also belong to any of the user's other channels) are auto-purged from the local database (in devices belonging to the user).

relations.subject: cbl:auto-purge-on-revoke
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted relation, version-gated breaking behavior change
relations.evidence: This is a Breaking Change at 3.0 ... Prior to this release, CBL auto-purged only in the case when the user loses access to a document by removing the doc from all of the channels belong to the user. Now, in addition to 2.x auto purge, Couchbase Lite will also auto-purges the docs when the user loses access to the doc via channel access revocation.

relations.subject: cbl:replication-filter
relations.evidence: Pull replication filters are not a substitute for channels. Sync Gateway channels are designed to be scalable (documents are filtered on the server) whereas a pull replication filter is applied to a document once it has been downloaded.

cross_product_finding: This page contains by far the richest set of genuinely access-control-shaped concepts found in this CBL batch, and they confirm the premise: CBL has NO server-side RBAC of its own. Its 'access control' story is entirely about (a) TLS-level server authentication (is this really Sync Gateway?), (b) client authentication credentials presented TO Sync Gateway (Basic/Session - not a privilege grant, just an identity proof), and (c) reactive, client-side auto-purge when Sync Gateway's own channel-based access control revokes a user's visibility into a document. Every actual authorization DECISION (who can see what) is made by Sync Gateway (channels, sync function, user authorization) - CBL only configures how to authenticate to it and how to react to its decisions. We minted stub concepts (cbl:sync-gateway, cbl:sync-gateway-channel) to represent this externally-owned system rather than reaching into the Sync Gateway batch's own extractions, per instructions not to reconcile across batches; a coordinator should link these stubs to whatever the Sync Gateway batch actually minted (we noticed, purely incidentally while inspecting the extractions directory, that a Sync Gateway batch has already minted 'sgw:channel', 'sgw:sync-function', etc., which look like strong reconciliation candidates for cbl:sync-gateway-channel). Separately, CBL's Basic/Session client-authenticator split is structurally reminiscent of Capella's 'credential-type-keyed privileges' (per the round-2 registry description) - both key some behavior off a named credential TYPE - but the resemblance is shallow: Capella's is about which privileges a credential type unlocks on a management plane, while CBL's is about which HTTP-level identity-proof mechanism the replicator uses; we did not reuse any Capella relation/concept for this since the shapes diverge beyond surface similarity. Finally, Delta Sync joins Predictive Query and Database Encryption as a third Enterprise-Edition-gated CBL feature, reinforcing that cbl:enterprise-edition is a real, recurring concept in this product though functionally unrelated to server/'s edition:enterprise gate set (GSI/eventing/etc.).
notable_absence: There is no CBL-side concept resembling a 'privilege', 'role', or 'grant' anywhere on this page - even the Enterprise Edition gate is a static, licensing-time feature toggle, not a runtime-checked permission. The only runtime-checked 'permission' in this whole flow (channel access) is Sync Gateway's, not CBL's.
